bibl.note: Arabic manuscript witness for textual comparison.

p.n: Sailors Depend on Ships and Vice Versa
The Cat Puts His Trust in the Rat

body.p:
“When the cat comprehended the talk by the rat, he knew that he was truthful and said to him,
‘Your words are, indeed, akin to the truth. I, too, am desirous of this truce, in which for you and for myself, I hope, will be deliverance. And if you
do this, I will thank you as long as I live.

p.n: The Rat Explains the Detail of the Last Rope

body.p:
The rat said: I shall approach you and cut
all your cords, except for one cord, which I shall keep to secure myself against you.’”

p.n: The Rat Begins to Cut the Rope

body.p: then took to gnawing at his cords.

p.n: The Cat Deems the Rat's Efforts Slow

body.p:
When the owl and the mongoose saw the rat approach the cat, they gave up on catching him and left. But the
rat held some speed from Rūmī while cutting the cords, so Rūmī said: ‘Why do I not see you being diligent at cutting my cords.
